title: Australia's Death Adder Strikes in 0.15 Seconds, After Waiting for Weeks
subject: death adder snake

scenes.text: Australia's fastest-striking snake almost never moves.
The death adder. It buries itself in leaf litter and can wait in one spot for days, even weeks.
Only the tip of its tail moves. It wriggles like a grub, right in front of its own head.
A lizard comes for the grub. The strike takes about 0.15 seconds, among the fastest ever measured in a snake, with the longest fangs in Australia.
It isn't a true adder at all. It's a cobra relative that learned to fish with its tail, and to wait.
Nothing moves but the tail. Until everything does.

description:
Australia's death adder has one of the fastest strikes ever measured in a snake, about 0.15 seconds, yet it spends its life lying still.
It hides in leaf litter for days or weeks, wriggling the grub-like tip of its tail as a lure until a lizard or bird comes close. Despite the name it is not a viper but a relative of cobras, and it has the longest fangs of any Australian snake.
Would you spot it before it spotted you?
first_comment: Bonus: because it waits instead of fleeing, people used to step on it, which is how it got its name. Which ambush predator would you least like to walk past?
